$comment: Scoped exceptions for banned-terms.json. Each entry suppresses hits on files whose repo-relative path CONTAINS `path` (a plain substring, not a glob). Omit `terms` to allowlist every banned term at that path; scope it to specific terms when the file is legitimate for one wave's word but would be a real hit for a later wave's. Keep entries file- or directory-scoped and explain the domain reason — this file is the audit trail for every 'connection' the gate lets through.

entries.reason: The /connections page itself — Connections is the word's one legitimate domain (plan D2).
Connectors entity layer backing the Connections page (OAuth connect flow, ConnectDialog copy).

The Messaging region of the /connections page (DOR-857). "Remove this connection?" names the entity a person is deleting — one Telegram bot or Slack app they set up — which is exactly what Connections means. Not the network-health sense DOR-855 retires: whether that connection is currently reachable is reported separately ("Reachable" / "Not reachable", per TestStep).

computeHealthState()'s "N connection(s) active/disconnected" and "No connections configured" count configured relay adapters (Telegram, Slack, webhook instances) — each adapter IS a Connection entity on the /connections page. This is the entity noun, not a network-health reading of whether a link is up; the adapter's own reachability is reported separately ("Reachable"/"Not reachable", per TestStep).

Two senses coexist here pending copy review: the Mesh Topology feature's "every connection" describes graph edges between agents, not link health; the Accounts feature's "Attach a connection to one session" is Connections-domain (an attached account). Neither is the network-health sense DOR-855 retires. Revisit if this file grows a true network-status blurb.
Marketing visual-design sandbox routes (hero/diagram prototypes) — "connection lines" describes SVG graph edges in a prototype, not shipped product copy.

MCP tool titles "List/Turn a chat connection on/off/Reload chat connections" describe relay adapters (Telegram/Slack) — the same Connections-domain entity as RelayHealthBar, surfaced to the agent rather than the human.

The `mcp_add` tool description tells an agent to read `connection.authKind` off the entry the call returns. That is a literal property path on the shipped MCP-server-entry shape (`agent-mcp-server-service.ts` reads `existing.connection.authKind`), addressed to a machine that will parse it — not the network-health sense DOR-855 retires. Rewriting the word here would make the description name a field that does not exist, so this is allowlisted rather than reworded, exactly as openapi-registry.ts is for the same reason.
"Your saved {provider} connection didn't work" reports a stale/invalid stored credential for a model provider — Connections-domain (an attached provider account), not a network-reachability reading.

OpenAPI `description` fields for the /api/docs developer reference, describing the MCP client's connection config and an attached account's connection details (spec security language) — Connections-domain API documentation, not cockpit network-status copy.

The Settings Tools tab group label "Connection management" (plan D4) names the tools that set up and route the Telegram/Slack/webhook Connections — the same Connections-domain entity as RelayHealthBar and mcp-tool-tiers, not the network-health sense DOR-855 retires.

The session-origin badge label "Connection" (plan D2, DOR-859) marks a session started by an inbound Telegram/Slack message — it names the Connections-domain entity that reached the agent, not whether a network link is up. The origin's health is never shown here.

The add/edit-binding dialog's "Add connection" / "Edit connection" / "Remove connection" copy (plan D2, DOR-859) names the entity a person is creating or deleting — one binding of a Telegram/Slack/webhook to an agent, which is exactly what a Connection is. Not the network-health sense DOR-855 retires; a binding's reachability is reported separately by its test action.

The per-agent Connections tab's toasts ("Connection added/removed/paused") and its "Add a connection" copy (plan D2, DOR-859) name the Connections-domain entity — a Telegram/Slack/webhook binding for this agent — not a network-health reading. Whether a binding is currently reachable is reported by its own test action, not this copy.

The per-agent Connections tab's picker "Add connection" button and "No connections available" empty state (plan D2, DOR-859) name the Connections-domain entity — a Telegram/Slack/webhook binding for this agent — not a network-health reading.

The per-agent Connections tab's binding card "Remove connection" confirmation (plan D2, DOR-859) names the Connections-domain entity a person is deleting — one Telegram/Slack/webhook binding — not a network-health reading.

The topology graph's adapter-node badge ("1 connection" / "N connections", plan D2, DOR-896) counts bindings attached to that adapter — the Connections-domain entity, same count IntegrationBindingCard and RelayHealthBar report elsewhere. Not a network-health reading.

The topology graph's binding-edge "Remove connection" aria-label (plan D2, DOR-896) names the Connections-domain entity a person is deleting — one adapter-to-agent binding — the same action IntegrationBindingCard's confirm dialog names elsewhere. The edge's own fallback display label ('Connection', in resolveDisplayLabel) is the same entity name but isn't a copy-bearing position the gate's static scan reaches (a bare `return` — the documented gap in check-vocab-gate.ts's module doc), so it needs no entry, only this note for the audit trail.

The topology graph's keyboard-fallback summary, drag-to-bind hint, and remove-binding confirm dialog (plan D2, DOR-896) all name the same Connections-domain entity as BindingEdge and AdapterNode in this directory: an adapter-to-agent binding a person creates or deletes. Not a network-health reading — a binding's own reachability is reported by its test action, not this copy.

The GitHub Agent HQ compare page's FAQ answers the question "What is GitHub Mission Control?" — GitHub's own blog named its agent-hub page that, and the FAQ says so exactly to note the docs don't use the name. AGENTS.md carves this out: GitHub ships a product literally named Mission Control. This is DorkOS's own carve-out, not the copy this wave retires.

The Messaging region's empty state (DOR-1754). "Connections let people and platforms reach your agents" and its "Add a connection" button name the Connections-domain entity a person is about to create, which is what this screen is for. Not the network-health sense DOR-855 retires.
The setup guide for one Telegram/Slack/webhook connection (DOR-1754) — "instructions for setting up this connection" names the entity being set up, not whether a link is up.
"N bindings already exist for this connection" (DOR-1754) counts routes attached to one Telegram/Slack connection — the same entity AdapterNode and RelayHealthBar count elsewhere.

The connection card and its parts (DOR-1754): "Connection actions", "Add connection", and the "Connection added" toast all name one Telegram/Slack/webhook a person set up — the Connections-domain entity MessagingConnections lists. The card reports reachability separately, in its own words.

The add-a-connection wizard (DOR-1754). "Connection ID" and the name field's helper text describe the entity being created; the wizard's own test step reports reachability in the plain-language family DOR-855 moved to.
The "Connection removed" toast (DOR-1754) reports the deletion of one Telegram/Slack/webhook — the same entity, and the same wording, as the per-agent Connections tab's toasts in IntegrationsTab.tsx.
"This connection is set to X" (DOR-1754) names the binding whose permission mode is on screen — the same entity BindingDialog's own copy names one layer up. Not a network-health reading.

The "Connection management" context block (DOR-1754) is the per-agent twin of the Settings Tools tab group in tool-inventory.ts, allowlisted for the same reason: it names the tools that set up and route Telegram/Slack/webhook Connections.
The per-agent "Connection management" tool group (DOR-1754) — the same group, under the same name, as tool-inventory.ts's, which is allowlisted for the same domain reason.
